_comment: Dominic Pizza (slug dominic-pizza), York — LumiPOS customer (full EPOS on a Sunmi T2: counter sales, cash drawer, Z report). NOT YET REBRANDED. Every value below is still Acomb Pizza & Kebab House's, copied wholesale from data/shops/acomb-pizza-kebab on 17 Sep 2026 so the Cloudflare project could be stood up and the T2 installed before Dominic's own details arrived. See _comment_rebrand.
_comment_rebrand: MUST ALL CHANGE BEFORE THIS SHOP TAKES A REAL ORDER. Still Acomb's: tradingName, shortName, the whole address block, phone, email, domain, logo.png, assets/, index.html (the landing page is built around Acomb's reference visual), order.css, and every one of the 141 menu items in menu.json + menu-visual.json. prelaunch is ON so none of it can reach Google in the meantime. The build already warns about legalName, companyNumber and stripe.connectedAccountId because those were never filled in for Acomb either - do not read a quiet build as a finished rebrand, because the fields that are WRONG rather than missing cannot warn.
_comment_product: LumiPOS, unlike Acomb which is LumiWEB. pos.ordersOnly has been REMOVED from the copy: Dominic is buying the full EPOS, so the T2 must show the counter mode bar and the card-reader tile. Leaving Acomb's ordersOnly:true would have hidden the counter sales this shop is paying ~£35/wk for. See docs/PRODUCTS.md.

business._comment_shortName: Conversational short form used in page headers, aria labels and the staff PWA name (e.g. 'Pizza Bob's' instead of 'Pizza Bob's Burgers Ltd').

_comment_theme: Brand red and gold sampled from the owner's reference visual. background/surface are the PLATFORM's light surfaces and must stay light: order.html, thank-you.html, reset-password, privacy, terms, allergy-info, the staff manifest and the confirmation email all paint dark ink on them without checking. They were briefly set to this shop's near-black, which rendered every one of those dark-on-dark — invisible headings on the thank-you page and invisible body text in the confirmation email. The DARK landing page is bespoke (data/shops/acomb-pizza-kebab/index.html) and now hardcodes its own #0a0a0a / #141414 rather than borrowing these. chrome stays dark so the staff PWA's theme_color is unchanged.

theme._comment_palette: Reds and cream sampled from the owner's logo artwork (_source/dominic-logo.png), not eyeballed: #E7151A is the most common exact red in the file and #FBF6E8 the most common cream. primaryDark and primaryDeep are darker steps of that same red for hovers and headings. The accent is still Acomb's gold (#c9a227) - the logo's only other colour is the Italian-flag green #036B3A, and swapping gold for green across a red-and-black site is a design call, not a colour correction.

delivery._comment_source: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER, 17 Sep 2026, from their live provider's own zone definitions. Three concentric circles on one centre, so the distances are STRAIGHT-LINE: 3226.36 m = 2.00 miles, 6469.95 m = 4.02 miles, 11332.72 m = 7.04 miles. Replaces Acomb's inherited hand-drawn polygons over Acomb and Poppleton, which were the far side of York from Lawrence Street.
delivery._comment_radius: roadFactor is deliberately ABSENT (defaults to 1, pure straight-line). The shop's own zones are circles on a map, so their current area IS crow-flies; applying the ~1.3 road factor used at Rico's would shrink the area they deliver to today and start refusing addresses they currently serve. origin is their zones' exact centre rather than a geocode of the postcode, so the boundary matches theirs to the metre.

radius._comment_bands: minOrderPence is PER BAND: £10 inside 4 miles, £20 out to 7, exactly as the owner has it. resolveDelivery returns the matched band's minimum and both the order page and computeTotals prefer it over minimumOrderPence below.

delivery._comment_minimum: The FALLBACK only — every band above sets its own, so this is what applies if a band ever loses its minOrderPence. £10, the nearest band's figure, so a lapse can only ever be more generous than intended rather than turning customers away. minimumIncludesFees is absent, i.e. false, so the minimum is measured on the basket BEFORE the delivery and service fees - a £9 basket is refused rather than being nudged over the line by charges the customer did not choose.
delivery._comment_minimumBeforeDiscount: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER, 17 Sep 2026: measure the delivery minimum on the subtotal BEFORE the 20% online discount, matching the ordering system they came from (whose promo threshold is also read off the gross subtotal). So £20 means £20 of menu items. Without it the 7-mile band's real minimum would be £25.00 - a £24.60 basket nets £19.68 after the discount and would be refused. Default (absent) keeps the after-discount behaviour, so Rico's and Big Bites are untouched.

_comment_serviceFee: Per-order platform fee in pence. Charged to the customer and kept by the platform.
_comment_stripe: Stripe Connect: this site's PaymentIntents are created on the venue's connected account. connectedAccountId is the venue's acct_xxx string from Stripe Connect.

hours._comment: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER, 17 Sep 2026: 4pm-3am every day, no closed day. 27:00 is 03:00 the NEXT morning - hours.js reads any close past 24:00 as rolling over, and 27:00 is the latest in the estate (the previous high-water mark was 25:00). ordering.businessDayStartHour stays 4, so the trading day runs 4am-4am and a 2am order is still counted against the night it belongs to.

ordering._comment_businessDayStartHour: Trading-day rollover hour (0–23, shop local time). 4 = the day's orders / takings / Z-report run 4am-to-4am, so a late-night shop's orders taken after midnight still count toward the day it opened. Set 0 for a plain midnight-to-midnight day. Safe to leave at 4 even for daytime shops (if you close before midnight there's nothing in the 0–4am window to reclassify).
ordering._comment_prep: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER, 17 Sep 2026: 20 minutes for collection, 45 for delivery (their provider's own auto-accept delivery time). asapMinPrepMinutes is the base and applies to collection; asapMinPrepMinutesByMode overrides it per mode. It sets the "As soon as possible (~N min)" label AND the earliest bookable slot, and /api/order enforces the same number, so the promise and the rule cannot drift. 25 was Acomb's inherited value.

_comment_promo: Standing offer agreed with the owner: 10% off EVERY online order with a subtotal of £12 or more (not a first-order welcome offer). minSubtotalPence is tested on the SUBTOTAL, before service fee and delivery. firstOrders stays off — the two do not stack and firstOrders would take precedence.

autoOnlineDiscount.label: 20% off online orders of £15 or more

promo._comment_autoOnlineDiscount: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER, 17 Sep 2026: 20% off the whole order, £15 or more (was Acomb's 10% over £12). Worded 'or more' rather than 'over' because the test is `subtotalP >= minSubtotalPence` in totals.js, so a basket of exactly £15.00 DOES qualify — and the shop's previous provider stated the same condition as “Sub-Total: greater than or equal to £15.00”. percent and minSubtotalPence are the ONLY source of truth: totals.js applies them server-side and the landing page renders them through the {{promoPercentText}} / {{promoMinimumText}} tokens, so the advertised offer cannot drift from the one given. The minimum is measured on the SUBTOTAL, before the service fee and delivery. NO menu item carries noPromo: the owner confirmed on 17 Sep 2026 that the Special Offers bundles get the discount too on their existing page, so the 20% comes off the whole basket including the meal deals. See NO_PROMO_CATEGORIES in tools/_gen-dominic-menu.py.

_comment_pos: Till behaviour flags (all optional, default off). requireOrderPin:true makes staff enter their operator code to START every order (walk-in/collection/delivery) — leave it false so staff take orders with no per-order PIN. NOTE: the manager/owner PIN on voids, refunds and cancellations is a SEPARATE gate and is ALWAYS required regardless of this flag. selfServeDrinks:true hides the till's drink picker; externalCardMachine:true marks the Card button as paid immediately for a shop using its own card terminal.

pos._comment_customerLookup: Staff see who is calling. With caller ID on the till, a number alone tells you nothing — this is the half that turns it into a name and their last address. It switches on TWO things that share one address book in CUSTOMERS_KV, keyed by normalised phone: /api/staff/customer-lookup (404s without this flag, which is why Dominic's first test call popped up a bare number), and the REMEMBERING that feeds it — every phone order taken on the till and every website order now leaves a contact record for that number. Contact records only: no password, no account, and an existing name is never overwritten. A brand-new shop has no phone-order history, so the website is the only thing that can fill the book in the first weeks; without it caller ID would show bare numbers until the shop had hand-typed enough orders. Off for every other shop, which stores nothing.
pos._comment_externalCardMachine: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER, 18 Sep 2026: Dominic takes card on their OWN third-party terminal, so there is no LumiPOS/Stripe reader to drive. externalCardMachine:true makes the till's Card button RECORD the sale as paid by card immediately — the counter sale, paying off an existing order, and the card half of a split all book straight away instead of waiting on a reader. Server-gated in counter-order.js and orders/[id]/pay.js, so it cannot be abused at a shop that does use a reader, and the till only skips the overlay. Without it, pressing Card here would fail outright with "Card payments are not configured for this shop", because stripe.connectedAccountId is still a placeholder. ⚠️ REFUNDS on a counter card sale must be done on the shop's OWN machine. LumiPOS never touched that money, so the till will correctly say there is no refundable payment; cancelling the order still works. This does NOT affect the website — online card payments still go through Stripe as normal once the connected account is set. Same setup as Big Bites and One Sip.
pos._comment_callerId: The shop's handset plugs into the FRITZ!Box FON port, so there is NO analogue line for a USB caller-ID modem to read — the router does the telephony. mode 'fritzbox' makes the till listen to the router's own call monitor over the LAN (plain TCP, port 1012) instead, and the number arrives as the same event, so the call bar and the customer lookup are unchanged. host is SET EXPLICITLY and must stay set: the plugin's fallback is this device's DHCP gateway, and reading that needs ACCESS_WIFI_STATE, which the first APK did not declare — the T2 logged 'gateway lookup failed: … ACCESS_WIFI_STATE' and never opened the socket. An explicit host skips that call entirely, so caller ID works on the APK already installed. It is also the more correct value here: the handsets hang off the FRITZ!Box but the till is on the separate WiFi box, whose DHCP gateway is not necessarily the FRITZ!Box. 192.168.178.1 was measured on site (17 Sep 2026) — 'nc -v 192.168.178.1 1012' connected and returned live ;RING; lines. If the router is ever replaced or its LAN subnet changed, this needs changing with it. ⚠️ SOMEONE MUST DIAL #96*5* ON A HANDSET CONNECTED TO THE FRITZ!BOX ONCE - that is what opens port 1012. It survives reboots but not a factory reset (#96*4* turns it off again). ⚠️ Caller ID is NATIVE code, so Capgo cannot deliver it: the T2 needs an APK built from commit e1f746b or later. host/port, though, come from THIS file over /api/config, so changing them needs only a redeploy and an app restart.

payments._comment_cvcThreshold: Order total (in pence) above which a customer paying with a saved card has to re-enter their CVV. Defends against account-takeover for higher-value orders. Set to 0 to never require CVC re-collection. £50 = 5000.

allergens.noticeAtCheckout: For allergens please contact the restaurant before ordering.

marketing._comment_metaPixelId: Meta (Facebook) Pixel ID from Events Manager (a numeric string). Set it to enable Facebook/Instagram ad conversion tracking: PageView on every customer page + Purchase on the thank-you page. Leave empty to keep the pixel off.

_comment_prelaunch: KEEPS THIS SHOP OUT OF GOOGLE. Every page sends X-Robots-Tag: noindex and robots.txt is Disallow-all. Non-negotiable while the site still carries Acomb Pizza & Kebab House's name, address and phone on a domain that is not theirs - indexing that would put a real shop's details under another shop's brand. Remove ONLY once the rebrand in _comment_rebrand is done.
_comment_seo: NO seo block - inherited from Acomb, which never had one. Before launch add cuisine, priceRange, addressRegion, description and ogImage, plus seo.geo {lat,lng} taken from the owner or Google Maps for the real shop. NEVER guess the coordinates: they are what puts Google's pin on the door.
